items.text: Planned tinydb YAMLStorage (to be built in a later session) decision, 2026-11-03: use PyYAML only, with no ruamel.yaml extra dependency. Plain yaml.safe_load was rejected (the agent had initially proposed it) because YAML 1.1 turns values like `country: NO` and `maintenance: off` into booleans, and ops team hand-edits files with such values. Only `true`/`false` may load as booleans; NO, off, yes must stay strings. Proposed approach: a SafeLoader subclass with its own copy of the implicit resolvers, the bool resolver replaced by a regex matching only true/false, leaving the global SafeLoader untouched. Open question: whether `True`/`TRUE` are accepted (agent leans lowercase only).

items.text: 3.x series highlights: v3.13.0 added direct storage access (#258), v3.14.0 deprecated ujson support, v3.15.0 allowed setting default table args (#278, #279). Table.update and Table.remove skip missing doc_ids instead of raising KeyError (May 2026, #616, fixes #591). IDs are filtered inside the updater so operations are atomic, avoiding half-applied in-place updates since documents are shared by reference; upsert dropped its unreachable except KeyError branch. items.text: Query cache documentation was added in 2020 (#320), explaining caching, unlimited cache size and memory usage, and the possibility of stale results, to warn users about query cache behavior. Docs builds were also extended with PDF/ePub output and a read-the-docs configuration.

Docs initiatives in August 2026: an architecture overview with a Mermaid-generated class diagram (architecture.mmd is the source of truth) in the API reference (#620, related #575); an explanation that Document instances retain doc_id when moved between tables/databases, with a dict(document) workaround (#622, #354); a caveat that Table.search() results share objects with the query cache (#617, fixes #516). The caveat is documented rather than fixed because a deep copy would cost 150-4000x on the read hot path.

TinyDB's doc_id handling has been refined over time: `insert_multiple` accepts `Document` instances (builds on #389), `Table.get` by doc_id is O(1) (#460), `Table.delete()` prefers `doc_ids` over `cond` for consistency (#424), and `upsert()` handles doc_id (#395, #394). In 2023 (May–June) `Table.get` gained a `doc_ids` parameter (#486, #504) and it was documented.

items.text: Internal convention (commit e23b831, Claus Aichinger, 2018-10-30): type checks were generalized from isinstance-dict to isinstance-Mapping so the code accepts any Mapping rather than only dict.

Releases after 4.0: v4.1.0 (2020-05-07) added a `noop` query operation (#313), fixed next document ID calculation on existing tables (#314), and added an `access_mode` flag to JSONStorage (#297). v4.1.1 followed on 2020-05-08, and v4.2.0 (2020-10-03) included custom doc_ids on insertion (#303) and a refactor to use OrderedDict.move_to_end() (#340, closes #338).

Storage/cache/ID correctness fixes in September 2026: CachingMiddleware rejects reads and writes after close (#634); insert_multiple no longer reuses IDs in mixed batches, with _next_id typed Optional[int] (#633); LRUCache get/__getitem__ use a private sentinel so stored None values are not treated as missing (#635). Earlier LRUCache fixes handled falsy values and LRUCache.set updating existing keys.
Python version support: Python 3.5 was dropped in May 2021 and Python 3.6 in January 2023; Python 3.10 support was added (#431), 3.9 testing added, and CI switched to PyPy 3.9.

items.text: TinyDB v4.0.0 was released on 2020-05-02 after a Table refactor: next ID is stored instead of last ID, process_docs removed, internal read/update methods renamed, `len(table)` faster, `Table.contains` restricted to a single doc ID (list was ambiguous), default table name and default cache capacity made configurable, and queries without a test dropped via breaking change `refactor(queries)!`. Upgrade notes and a changelog were written; follow-up fixes covered ID generation, `len(db)` on empty databases (#307), and document ID conversion in updates.

TinyDB v3.12.0 was released on November 6, 2018 (version bump by Markus Siemens), followed by v3.12.1 on November 9, 2018. v3.12.1 included the fix 'Don't break when searching the same query multiple times' (commit d69d6f4, Andrew Reilly, 2018-11-09), which repaired repeated identical queries breaking search.

TinyDB documentation and extension list curation (2025-12 to 2026-10): unsupported extensions (tinymongo, TinyMP, TinyDBTimestamps, tinyindex) were removed and listing requirements stated; tinydbjoin and tinydbstorage were added (#647); tinydb-rust was added earlier and extension statuses updated. A security policy with callable-safety notes, AI assistance guidelines, and a project status note were also added to set contributor and security expectations.

Atomic writes to avoid data corruption on crashes were added to storage (#468) with Windows support, then reverted in May 2022 because of a CI failure. CI was expanded to macOS and Windows, excluding Windows+PyPy3 and macOS+PyPy3.

The default table name and default cache capacity were made configurable, and queries without a test were dropped via the breaking change `refactor(queries)!`. Upgrade notes and a changelog for 4.0 were written. Follow-up fixes covered ID generation, `len(db)` on empty databases (#307), and document ID conversion in updates. | When: 2020-01-02 to 2020-05-02 | Involving: Markus Siemens | Simplify the API and make method semantics clear

items.text: October 2026 bug-fix wave in TinyDB Query/Table: Query.any/all no longer treat str/bytes/bytearray as sequences (is_sequence now uses collections.abc.Sequence) (#641, fixes #638); regex flags are included in matches/search query hash so the query cache no longer conflates case-sensitive and insensitive searches (#640, fixes #637); persist_empty=True no longer wipes existing table data on reopen (#642, fixes #636). | When: 2026-10-06 | Involving: Utkarsh Adhran | Correctness bugs in query matching, query cache and empty-table persistence
